note: Facts for every workflow and skill in the kit, except the four change-only ones. Each fact is taken from the item's own SKILL.md. gate and evidence are always lists. A line number points to that item's own SKILL.md.

workflows.name: requirements-workflow
workflows.what: The first workflow. It takes one product from its requirement files to an accepted PRD. It runs three skills in order, and stops at each one's gate. It writes nothing and decides nothing itself.
takesIn: in a change: section 15 of the Change impact report, for the steps to run
givesOut: Question log, through each of its skills
inFlow: It is the first workflow. Nothing comes before it.
It runs `scaffold-project.cjs` first.
Step 1: `discovery-author`, which runs `list-sources.cjs` first.
Step 2: `brd-author`.
Step 3: `prd-author`.
Next: `glossary-author`. In a change, the next row of the change's path.
It picks up at the first step whose document is not accepted yet. On a new project, that is step 1.
You can start it at a named step, such as "from prd-author".
In a change, it runs only the steps the change's path names: step 2 or step 3.
It adds nothing between the steps. Each skill runs `probing-questions-author` and `grade-questions.cjs` inside itself.
It is also the way to start the project again from nothing. This happens only when you ask for it in words, such as "start the project again from nothing".

When you start again from nothing, every file and folder in `Output/{project}/` except `sources/` moves to `_archive/Output-{date}/{project}/`. No program does this move yet: the workflow does it by hand. Then every step runs fresh.
gate: the skills' own: 3
Only when you ask to start again from nothing, it asks for your yes before step 1, as multiple choice.
Answer: Move them, and start again from nothing.
Answer: Keep the project as it is.
Answer: I don't know yet.
workflows.changeMode: It runs only the steps the change's path names, for the items it names, and gives each skill the change's number.

workflows.name: data-model-workflow
workflows.what: The workflow that turns the Glossary into the data model. It lists the things first, then writes one data model file for each Glossary family. Then it sends every Glossary change the data model found to the Glossary in one batch, and brings the data model in step with the answers.
takesIn: in a change: section 15 of the Change impact report, for the steps to run
givesOut: data model file, one for each family, through `data-model-author`
the data model's decisions file, through both skills
a ripple list of the documents that use each term, through `glossary-disposition`
the status mark of each Glossary change, in the data model's decisions file: the only thing the workflow writes itself
inFlow: It comes after `glossary-author`.
Step 1: `things-author`.
Step 2: `data-model-author`, once for each family the things file names.
Step 3: `glossary-disposition`, once, with every Glossary change as one batch. It runs only once every data model file is accepted.
Step 4: `things-author`, then `data-model-author`, each in a change, for the Glossary changes settled at step 3.
Next: `features-and-epics-workflow`. In a change, the next row of the change's path.
It says its mode first, in one sentence.
Mode: a change.
Mode: a new build.
Mode: picking up where it stopped.
Mode: nothing to do.
At every step, the skill first asks again each decision answered "I don't know yet", and each Glossary change left open, that it owns.
You can start it at a named step, for named files, such as "data-model-author, lending.md only".
In a change, it runs only the steps the change's path names: step 1 or step 2.
It marks each Glossary change as it goes, in this order.
Mark 1: "To raise".
Mark 2: "Raised".
Mark 3: "Settled in the Glossary on {date}". For "I don't know yet", it is "Left open on {date}" instead.
Mark 4: "Brought into the data model on {date}".
After each mark it writes, it runs `check-simple-writing.cjs` on the data model's decisions file.
A Glossary change is not a requirement change, so it never uses `requirement-update-workflow`.
It never sends anything back to the BRD or the PRD. Two requirements that disagree become a data model decision.
gate: the skills' own: 3
Step 4 holds the gates of `things-author` and `data-model-author` again, for what changed only.
When the batch at step 3 adds new words, `glossary-author` holds its own two gates for those words.
workflows.changeMode: It runs only the steps the change's path names, for the things and files it names, and gives each skill the change's number.

workflows.name: features-and-epics-workflow
workflows.what: The workflow after the data model. It takes the product from its PRD and its data model to its EPICs. It runs three skills and one program in order, and stops at each skill's gate.
takesIn: in a change: section 15 of the Change impact report, for the steps to run
inFlow: It comes after `data-model-workflow`, once every data model file is accepted.
It runs `scaffold-project.cjs` first.
Step 1: `feature-author`.
Step 2: `epic-grouping-author`.
Step 3: `epic-author`, in register mode, with its copy check, `check-register.cjs`. On a fail, back to step 3.
Step 4: `build-sequencing-mapping.cjs`, a program.
Next: `frd-workflow`. In a change, the next row of the change's path.
By default it starts at step 1. You can start it at a named step, for named items, such as "epic-grouping-author, place F-06 only".
In a change, it runs only the steps the change's path names: step 1, 2 or 3.
At step 1, when you pick "a new requirement first" for a row, `feature-author` runs only step 1 of `requirement-update-workflow`, at its gate.
A loop in the EPICs' dependencies, found at step 4, stops the run and goes back to step 2.
gate: the skills' own: 2
Step 3 has no gate: a pass of `check-register.cjs` is the acceptance.
Step 4 has no gate.
workflows.changeMode: It runs only the steps the change's path names, for the items it names, and gives each skill the change's number.

workflows.name: frd-workflow
workflows.what: The workflow that writes the FRDs, one FRD per run, in the order the EPICs are built. A program names the next capability. Then `frd-author` writes its FRD and holds its gate.
takesIn: in a change: section 15 of the Change impact report, for the FRDs to write
inFlow: It comes after `features-and-epics-workflow`, once the EPIC register is written.
It runs `scaffold-project.cjs` first.
Step 1: `route-next-capability.cjs`, a program. It names the next capability, in EPIC register order. A capability waiting on a Must answer question comes last, and a parked one after it.
Step 2: `frd-author`.
Next: run it again for the next capability.
`stories-workflow` can start on an EPIC once the FRDs of that EPIC's own features are accepted, even while other FRDs are open.
When every FRD is accepted, it prints "Every FRD accepted: next, run stories-workflow." and stops.
You can name a capability, such as "the FRD for Claim approval". Then it skips the routing.
In a change, it skips the routing and calls `frd-author` for each FRD the change's path names.
For an accepted FRD that waits on a data model answer now settled, it skips the routing and calls `frd-author` for that FRD.
A parked FRD ends the run. The next run routes to other work first.
gate: the skills' own: 1
workflows.changeMode: It skips the routing and calls `frd-author` for each FRD the change's path names, with the change's number.

workflows.name: stories-workflow
workflows.what: The workflow that takes one EPIC from its EPIC brief, if it has one, to stories ready to build. Two programs pick the EPIC and check whether it gets an EPIC brief. Then four skills run in order, each stopping at its gate.
takesIn: in a change: section 15 of the Change impact report, for the steps and stories to run
givesOut: EPIC brief, only for an EPIC that gets one, through `epic-author`
inFlow: It comes after `frd-workflow`, once the FRDs of the EPIC's own features are accepted. Another FRD may still be waiting or parked.
Step 1: `route-next-epic.cjs`, a program. It names the next EPIC that is not waiting on a parked one or on a Must answer question.
Then it runs `scaffold-project.cjs` for the EPIC's folder.
Step 2: `route-brief-list.cjs`, a program. It says yes or no: does this EPIC get an EPIC brief?
Step 3: `epic-author`, in brief mode, only on yes.
Step 4: `story-drafter`.
Step 5: `story-groomer`.
Step 6: `ac-author`.
Next: run it again for the next EPIC. When every EPIC is ready, it prints "Every EPIC ready." and stops.
You can name an EPIC, or start at a named step for named stories.
In a change, it runs only the steps the change's path names: step 3, 4, 5 or 6.
The ready guard: the stories can't be marked ready while a Must answer question raised in them is open. If one can't be answered yet, you can park the EPIC.
To put a ready story into a tracker, such as a GitHub issue, use `reader-copy.cjs`. It leaves out the citations. The Story file stays the agreed copy.
gate: the skills' own: 4
Step 3's gate runs only for an EPIC that gets an EPIC brief.
workflows.changeMode: It runs only the steps the change's path names, for the EPIC and stories it names. A story already marked ready is never changed: the difference becomes a new story, through `story-drafter`.

skills.name: probing-questions-author
skills.what: The skill that turns every gap in a document into a question for you. It rates each question's impact and severity, and writes it into the Question log. It never asks the questions or decides them.
takesIn: the document the calling skill just drafted
Question log, so a question is never asked twice
the requirement files the document cites
givesOut: Question log: new questions, and changes to open ones
inFlow: It runs inside every author skill, after the skill drafts and before its check program.
It never runs inside `things-author` or `data-model-author`. Their decisions stay in the data model's decisions file, never in the Question log.
It is never a workflow step of its own.
After it, `grade-questions.cjs` places each question in its group and sets the order. Inside a calling skill, the calling skill runs it.
Then it runs `check-simple-writing.cjs` on the Question log.
Inside a calling skill, it hands back each gap's place and its question's number. The calling skill writes them in.
It can run on its own, with a project and a document. Then it writes the numbers into a drafted document itself. For an accepted document, it lists each gap and its question for you instead.
When the project starts again from nothing, it raises every question fresh. It never asks an earlier question again.
gate: none: its questions are asked at the calling skill's gate

skills.name: discovery-author
skills.what: The skill that takes the first look at your requirement files and writes the Discovery brief. It lists every file, proposes which kind of file wins when two disagree, and compares what the files say topic by topic. Every clash, silence and assumption becomes a question.
takesIn: your requirement files, every file in `Output/{project}/sources/`
inFlow: It is step 1 of `requirements-workflow`, always the first step.
It runs `scaffold-project.cjs`, then `list-sources.cjs`.
It runs `probing-questions-author`, then `grade-questions.cjs`, then its check, `check-discovery-brief.cjs`.
When you accept, it runs `accept.cjs`, then `status.cjs`.
Next: `brd-author`, then `prd-author`. Only the files it marks Used are read after this step.
It runs once for each start of a project, and never in a change.
It can run on its own, with the project's name.
After a third "no", you can't park it, as it covers the whole product.
gate: Accept the Discovery brief?
Before it: the questions the brief raised, one at a time.
Before it: the order of authority.
Before it: each file proposed as out of scope.
skills.changeMode: It never runs in a change: a gap found later comes in as a change, through `requirement-update-workflow`.

takesIn: the requirement files the Discovery brief marks Used, and only those
in a change: the Change impact report
inFlow: It is step 2 of `requirements-workflow`.
It comes after `discovery-author`. It stops if the Discovery brief is missing or not accepted.
It works through its checklist, `references/brd-checklist.md`.
It runs `probing-questions-author`, then `grade-questions.cjs`, then its check, `check-brd.cjs`.
When you accept, it runs `accept.cjs`, then `status.cjs`.
Next: `prd-author`.
It can run on its own, with the project's name.
After a third "no", you can't park it, as it covers the whole product.
gate: Accept the BRD?
Before it: the questions the BRD raised or builds on, one at a time.
Before it: each objective and business requirement marked Proposed.
skills.changeMode: It reads the Change impact report too, changes only what it names, then holds its check and its gate again.

skills.name: prd-author
skills.what: The skill that records what the client asked for, one requirement per row, in simple words. Next to each row it keeps the part of the client's words it comes from, and its source. It also writes the personas, the end-to-end journey, the NFRs and the transition requirements.
takesIn: Discovery brief, for the order of authority and how each clash was settled
the requirement files the Discovery brief marks Used, and only those
Glossary, only when the project has one, for its agreed words
in a change: the Change impact report
in a change: the files you brought
inFlow: It is step 3 of `requirements-workflow`.
It comes after `brd-author`. It stops if the BRD is missing or not accepted.
It works through its checklist, `references/prd-checklist.md`.
It runs `probing-questions-author`, then `grade-questions.cjs`, then its check, `check-prd.cjs`.
When you accept, it runs `accept.cjs`, then `status.cjs`.
Next: `glossary-author`, then `data-model-workflow`, then `feature-author`.
It can run on its own, with the project's name.
After a third "no", you can't park it, as it covers the whole product.
gate: Do the simple words say the same as the client's words?
Are these rows not requirements? Asked only when a row's kind is not Requirement.
Accept the PRD?
Before them: the questions the PRD raised or builds on, one at a time.
Before them: each recommended NFR, one at a time.
skills.changeMode: It reads the Change impact report and the files you brought, changes only what the recommendation names, then holds its check and its gate again.

skills.name: glossary-author
skills.what: The skill that builds the Glossary: the one word the product uses for each meaning, its definition, and how the words relate. It holds two gates. Gate 1 settles the words, and Gate 2 settles the definitions.
takesIn: the existing Glossary, if any, with its working files in `glossary/deep-dives/`
in a change: the Change impact report, and only the requirements it names
when adding words from a request: each word, with its evidence
givesOut: its gate log, the only place a Glossary decision is written
Question log, for a gate row answered "I don't know yet", through `probing-questions-author`
inFlow: It runs on its own, between `requirements-workflow` and `data-model-workflow`. It is a skill, not a workflow.
It runs once the PRD is accepted. It stops if the PRD is not accepted.
It says its mode first, in one sentence.
Mode: a new build.
Mode: picking up where it stopped.
Mode: a re-run.
Mode: adding words from a request.
It runs `scaffold-project.cjs`, then shows where it will write, as a tree.
Before each gate, it runs `check-simple-writing.cjs`.
Before Gate 2, it runs `fill-also-written-as.cjs`.
After both gates, it runs `build-glossary-records.cjs`, then `build-retired-words-tables.cjs`.
It runs the method's character sweep and link check.
Last, it runs `accept.cjs` on the gate log.
`glossary-disposition` calls it, in its mode "add words from a request", with a batch of new words. It runs the whole batch in one run.
Next: `data-model-workflow`.
gate: Gate 1: one word for each meaning. Each gate row is one decision, asked on its own, such as: Do "cart" and "basket" mean the same thing? If so, which word does the glossary use?
Gate 2: each definition, one gate row at a time.
Neither gate passes while any row is open.
skills.changeMode: It reads the Change impact report too, and only the requirements it names.

skills.name: glossary-check
skills.what: The skill that finds where a document or story has drifted from the Glossary. It reports each place, with a recommended fix. It changes nothing.
takesIn: the document or story you share
givesOut: inside a change: the change's Check findings, `changes/{change}/check-findings.md`
on its own: a findings list, shown in the conversation
inFlow: It looks for four kinds of drift.
Drift 1: a retired word in use.
Drift 2: a term used against its definition.
Drift 3: a product word with no entry.
Drift 4: two words for one meaning.
Inside a change, it runs at step 3 of `requirement-update-workflow`. `glossary-disposition` runs next, when its findings hold a mismatch.
It hands its findings to `glossary-disposition`.
It stops if the Glossary's seven pages are missing. Then you run `glossary-author` first.
It can run on its own, with the project and the document.
gate: none
skills.changeMode: Inside a change, it saves its findings as the change's Check findings.

skills.name: glossary-disposition
skills.what: The skill that settles a mismatch between a document and the Glossary, or changes an agreed word. It settles one word at a time, at its gate. It edits the Glossary, never the documents that use a term: it lists them in a ripple list instead.
takesIn: Check findings, or your request to change a term
for a batch from the data model: every Glossary change the data model's decisions file marks "Raised"
givesOut: its gate log: a new Change part, rows CH-01 onward
a ripple list of the documents that use each term
Question log, for a word answered "I don't know yet", through `probing-questions-author`. Never for a batch from the data model.
inFlow: Inside a change, it runs at step 4 of `requirement-update-workflow`, after `glossary-check` and before `change-impact-author`.
It runs first in the Extend and Update paths of a change that renames an agreed word.
It runs at step 3 of `data-model-workflow`, once, with every Glossary change the data model raised, as one batch.
It sends each new word to `glossary-author`, in its mode "add words from a request". For a batch from the data model, every new word goes together, in one run.
It runs `build-glossary-records.cjs`, then `build-retired-words-tables.cjs`.
It runs `check-simple-writing.cjs`, and the method's character sweep and link check.
Last, it runs `accept.cjs` on the gate log.
For a batch from the data model, it reports each change's outcome to `data-model-workflow`.
It can run on its own, with a word to change, such as "rename claim to expense claim".
gate: How should each mismatched word be settled? Asked one word at a time.
For a batch from the data model: How should the Glossary settle this change? Asked for each change on its own. It never offers "fix the document".
skills.changeMode: Inside a change, it runs before `change-impact-author`, so the change is weighed in agreed words.

Mode: nothing to do.

Accept the things?

givesOut: data model file, one for this family, such as `lending.md`
the data model's decisions file: this file's decisions and Glossary changes

It never runs `probing-questions-author`. Its decisions stay in the data model's decisions file, never in the Question log.

When you accept, it runs `accept.cjs`, then `status.cjs`.
Next: the next family. After the last family, `glossary-disposition`, at step 3 of `data-model-workflow`.
Later, `feature-author` and `frd-author` read its file.
It can run on its own, with the project's name and the family.

Accept the {family name} data model?

After a third "no", you may park the FRD, with `park.cjs`.
gate: Accept the FRD?
First, the Must answer questions it builds on, one at a time. While one is open, the FRD can't be accepted: you answer it, or park the FRD.
Before it: the other questions, in order.
Before it: each suggested rule, as keep or drop, one at a time.
skills.changeMode: It reads the Change impact report too and changes only what it names. Rule IDs already accepted never change.

skills.name: story-drafter
skills.what: The skill that splits one EPIC into user stories, in the order they are worked. Each story is a title and an "As a / I want / So that" statement, one capability each. The Story files are made only after you approve the split.
takesIn: EPIC brief, if the EPIC has one
in a change: the Change impact report
givesOut: Stories: one Story file for each story, made only after you approve the split
inFlow: It is step 4 of `stories-workflow`, after step 2 or step 3.
It runs `scaffold-project.cjs` for the EPIC. It stops if an FRD the EPIC's features need is not accepted.
It runs `probing-questions-author`, then `grade-questions.cjs`, then its check, `check-stories.cjs`.
When you approve, it makes the Story files, runs the check again, then runs `accept.cjs` and `status.cjs`.
Next: `story-groomer`.
It can run on its own, with the project's name and the EPIC.
After a third "no", you may park the EPIC.
gate: Approve the split? One gate for all the EPIC's stories together, with their order.
Before it: the questions, in order.
skills.changeMode: It changes only what the Change impact report names. Each story keeps its title and place, and a new story goes at the end of the list. A story already ready is never changed.

skills.name: story-groomer
skills.what: The skill that grooms every story of one EPIC, only from documents already decided. For each story it writes its dependencies, its scope in and out, and the FRD rules it delivers, quoted by ID. It decides no rules: a gap becomes a question.
takesIn: in a change: the Change impact report
givesOut: Stories: each one's grooming sections, from Dependencies to Design links
Stories and Story list: each story's status, groomed
inFlow: It is step 5 of `stories-workflow`, after `story-drafter`.
It stops if the EPIC's split is not approved.
It runs `probing-questions-author`, then `grade-questions.cjs`, then its check, `check-stories.cjs`.
When you accept, it runs the check again, then `accept.cjs`, then `status.cjs`.
Next: `ac-author`.
It can run on its own, with the project's name and the EPIC.
After a third "no", you may park the EPIC.
gate: Accept the grooming? One gate for all the EPIC's stories together.
Before it: the questions, in order.
skills.changeMode: It changes only the grooming the Change impact report names. A story already ready is never groomed again: the difference comes as a new story, through `story-drafter`.

skills.name: ac-author
skills.what: The skill that writes the acceptance criteria for every story of one EPIC: three to seven Given, When, Then scenarios each. Every scenario names the FRD rules it proves, and every rule of the EPIC's features must be proved. On acceptance, it marks the stories ready.
takesIn: in a change: the Change impact report
givesOut: Stories: each one's Acceptance criteria section
Stories and Story list: each story's status, ready
inFlow: It is step 6 of `stories-workflow`, the last step, after `story-groomer`.
It stops if the EPIC's grooming is not accepted.
It runs `probing-questions-author`, then `grade-questions.cjs`.
Its checks are `check-stories.cjs`, then `coverage-check.cjs`.
When you accept, it runs `accept.cjs`, then `status.cjs`.
Next: `stories-workflow` routes to the next EPIC.
It can run on its own, with the project's name and the EPIC.
After a third "no", you may park the EPIC.
gate: Accept the criteria? This marks the stories ready.
First, the ready guard: each Must answer question raised in these stories, one at a time. While one is open, the stories can't be marked ready.
Before it: the other questions, in order.
skills.changeMode: It changes only the scenarios the Change impact report names, and adds one for each rule the change adds or changes. Every other scenario stays word for word.
